UX-2 · quick look before any prototype · proposal · 2026-10-20

A6 · Branch office

The Customer Service Workspace look you pointed at: a navy band, a pale grey page, white cards with a soft shadow, one bank blue for every action, and plain grey label-value grids. The staff console follows the shot closely; the homeowner chat is the translation (see "Turning a workspace into a chatbot" in docs/design/DESIGN-DIRECTIONS.md § A6). Same four screens and the same words as the A4 and A5 sheets, plus one plain chat turn. Nothing here is clickable; the prototype gets built only after you pick. Fonts load from Google Fonts with a system fallback.

A5 vs A6: the same handoff card

A5 is the other direction still in play. Same card, same words, both light.

Mockups in light mode (the primary theme)

A plain chat turn with its source · booking a window · the handoff with its honest promise · the safety card (the only square, red object) · the staff case view.

Palette (sampled from the shots; UX-3 makes it exact)

Sampled with Pillow from dr-35: page #F7F7F7, cards #FFFFFF, band #002A54, assistant panel #013A6F, buttons and links #056DAE, staff bubble #DBDBDB with text #565656, every other text #666666. All of the shot's text already passes AA, so text is unchanged. Two things fail as drawn: its light-blue button edge #C0DAEB (1.45:1) and its pale field borders, so control edges use #8C8C8C or the blue itself. The selected tint #E4EEF8 comes from dr-40. Red only for safety. The build fails if any text pair is under 4.5:1 or a control edge under 3:1.
